instruction_format.rule: Every instruction is expressed as a TARGET END STATE ('hold 0.0091 ETH'), never as a delta ('sell 0.0273 ETH'). End states are idempotent: safe to act on whether or not a previous instruction was executed.

stop_trigger_rule.rule: A stop is triggered by a DAILY CLOSE below the level, not by an intraday print. Same for targets.
why: ETH is the only position whose trigger condition was ever written down, and it says 'if price CLOSES below the stop, convert ALL to USDT'. This makes the book consistent rather than inventing a new convention.
The stop LEVEL is computed from daily closes (close - 3 x ATR14). A level derived from closes but triggered intraday is internally inconsistent.

Decisive: this system observes prices ONCE a day at 07:10 UTC and notifies once a day. An intraday stop is not executable here - claiming an exit at 11.337 would mean claiming a fill at a price nobody observed and nobody could have acted on. That is the August bookkeeping failure repeating.
stop_trigger_rule.honesty_note: This is being written down AFTER the ambiguous event, and it resolves in the direction that keeps the LINK position alive. That is uncomfortable and is recorded rather than glossed. The three reasons above are outcome-independent, and the rule now binds in both directions: a close below a stop exits even if the position recovers intraday afterwards.
stop_trigger_rule.cost_disclosed: A close-based stop does NOT fill at the stop level. With one observation a day, the exit happens at the next daily reading, which can be well below the stop. Yesterday I wrote 'if it fires it fires near +17.1%' - that was imprecise, and the realistic fill is worse than the level.

stretch_watch.outcome: Yesterday six of eleven cryptos carried stretch penalties and I wrote that the engine was flagging extension rather than weakness, and that the easy part of the move had happened. Today the board fell and the stretched alts fell hardest - AVAX (RSI 79.8) -8.40%, XRP (70.1) -7.58%, DOGE (72.2) -7.55%, ADA (72.8) -6.78%. But the relationship is LOOSE, not clean, and overclaiming it would be the easy mistake: BTC was stretched at RSI 72.6 and fell only 2.73%, LINK was the least stretched of the big fallers at 64.3 and still fell 4.76%, and LTC - the second most stretched at 78.8 - was the ONLY green name on the board at +6.80%. Stretch ranked the downside directionally and got the extremes right, and it also completely missed the day's biggest single move. Treat it as one input among several, not a forecast.
